page: Vultr voc-m-4c-32gb-200s-amd is an AMD EPYC-based virtual server belonging to the Optimized Cloud Compute family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical x86_64 cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The processor includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, with support for AVX-512, AES, and SHA-NI instruction sets. The hardware configuration is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Local storage is provided by a bundled 200 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU hardware is present.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance placing in the top 10% and Geekbench single-core scores in the top 25%. Memory write bandwidth for large blocks is also strong, ranking in the top 25% at 113.08 GB/sec, alongside a strong PassMark memory score. However, multi-core scaling presents some limitations. Multi-core stress-ng and Geekbench scores fall into the average tier, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and PassMark database operations register in the bottom 25%. Static web serving throughput is also relatively low at 3.81 GB/sec, and LLM inference speeds for text generation on a 7B model are limited to 6.56 tokens/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance offers a high memory density relative to its compute footprint, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive multi-threaded CPU scaling. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent performance without resource contention. Given the high memory capacity and strong single-core performance, this server is suited for in-memory caching, memory-intensive data processing, text processing, and lightweight application hosting.
